component.name: Apache Tapestry
component.description: Component-based Java web application framework. Developers build pages and components; Tapestry handles request dispatch, rendering, form/event processing, asset serving, and serialization of some server-side state into the client (page activation context, form data) which it validates and deserializes on postback. The single most security-load-bearing mechanism is the HMAC-protected serialized client state: Tapestry round-trips serialized objects through the browser and deserializes them on return, so their integrity rests on a configured HMAC secret.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it. Draft under Tapestry PMC review with wave-1/2 maintainer answers folded in.

blueprints.name: Tapestry web application
blueprints.description: A servlet container hosts the Tapestry application; the trust boundary is the HTTP request: parameters, form data, activation context, and serialized client state are untrusted until validated. The application developer's pages, components, and handlers are trusted authored code.

assets.name: Serialized client state and HMAC gate
assets.description: t:formdata and activation serialization deserialized on postback, accepted only if its HMAC verifies against the configured tapestry.hmac-passphrase. The critical, attacker-reachable deserialization channel; its safety is entirely the HMAC (the post-CVE-2021-27850 design).

assets.name: Rendering and template output
assets.description: Component render and output escaping; the XSS surface.

assets.name: Asset serving
assets.description: Classpath/context asset URLs resolving to filesystem/classpath resources; the traversal surface.

assets.name: Access whitelisting
assets.description: @WhitelistAccessOnly pages/services gated by the ClientWhitelist analyzer, default LocalhostOnly (localhost IPv4/IPv6). An address/origin filter, not user authentication.

assets.name: Forms and file upload
assets.description: Form submit and multipart upload handling with temp files.

zones.name: Web clients
zones.description: Any browser or agent issuing requests, form posts, and activation-context URLs; untrusted.

zones.name: Tapestry application
zones.description: The framework and developer-authored application code in the servlet container; developer and operator are trusted.

persona.description: Untrusted primary adversary: submits crafted activation/event contexts, tampered or replayed serialized client state, malicious asset paths, oversized/typed uploads, and content intended to reflect as XSS. Goals: deserialization RCE via forged client state (defeated only by the HMAC), arbitrary file read via asset traversal, reaching a whitelisted/admin page, stored/reflected XSS, DoS via large uploads/contexts.
Authors pages, components, templates, and handlers and chooses where to use raw output, uploads, whitelisting, and HTTPS. Trusted; out of model as adversary.
Sets tapestry.hmac-passphrase, production mode, and deployment hardening. Trusted; out of model.

assumptions.description: A servlet container hosts the Tapestry application; TLS is provided by the container.
tapestry.hmac-passphrase is configured to a strong secret by the operator.
Production mode disables developer conveniences (detailed exception pages, component reload).
Tapestry reads classpath/context assets, writes temp files for uploads, and deserializes HMAC-validated client state; it is not assumed to open arbitrary sockets or run host commands.
Internal test code (src/test/** in every module), sample apps, and documentation do not deploy and are not an adversary surface.

threats.name: Deserialization RCE via forged serialized client state
threats.description: An attacker submits an arbitrary serialized object as client state; acceptance of a forged serialized object means remote code execution. Serialized client state is deserialized only after its HMAC verifies against the configured passphrase, the post-CVE-2021-27850 protection. Reports that ignore the HMAC gate are known non-findings; only an HMAC bypass (or an unset passphrase) is valid. Critical severity.

threats.name: XSS from framework-rendered values
threats.description: Reflected or stored XSS from values Tapestry itself renders; rendered component output is HTML-escaped by default, and the PMC notes any unchecked passthrough of data in an internal component should itself be treated as a bug. High to critical severity.

threats.name: Path traversal via asset URLs
threats.description: Reading files outside the asset roots through asset requests. Traversal is prevented by a mix of the servlet container's path normalization and Tapestry's own checks (explicit exclusion of sensitive file extensions); the PMC notes these checks could be improved further. Critical severity.

threats.name: Whitelisted page reachable by a non-whitelisted client
threats.description: @WhitelistAccessOnly resources served to a client outside the whitelist; by default only LocalhostOnly is contributed (localhost IPv4/IPv6). High severity. The PMC noted a correctness bug where certain shortened IPv6 addresses are falsely denied (TAP5-2832), which is over-restrictive, not a bypass. A whitelisted page reachable from localhost is by design.

threats.name: Secure page served over plain HTTP
threats.description: RequestSecurityManager decides whether HTTPS is required from a page's @Secure annotation; enforcement is on by default in production mode and configurable via tapestry.secure-enabled. A secure page served over plain HTTP is a medium to high severity violation.

threats.name: Denial of service via large uploads or contexts
threats.description: Upload-based DoS and content-type confusion through oversized or mistyped uploads and large activation/event contexts; the operator must set upload size/type limits.

threats.name: Deployment without a configured HMAC passphrase
threats.description: If tapestry.hmac-passphrase is unset or weak, the serialized-state protection is void and the deserialization surface reopens. An unset passphrase is currently a loud error (logged plus an AlertManager client-side alert), not yet a hard startup failure; making it fail closed in production mode is planned (TAP5-2834). Misconfiguration is the operator's responsibility.

threats.name: Cross-site request forgery on form/event posts
threats.description: Tapestry ships no CSRF module/component. The HMAC guards invalid requests, but a valid request is still subject to CSRF, so CSRF defence is the application's responsibility until a built-in lands (the PMC is planning one; prior art: porscheinformatik/tapestry-csrf-protection, primarily by a Tapestry committer/PMC member).

threats.name: XSS via developer-emitted raw output
threats.description: Raw output is an explicit opt-in via MarkupWriter.writeRaw or the OutputRaw component, where the developer must escape/validate beforehand; XSS attributed to a developer's raw output of untrusted data is the developer's responsibility, not a framework default.

threats.name: Information disclosure from development mode in production
threats.description: Running in development mode in production exposes detailed exception pages and component sources; dev-mode information disclosure against a dev configuration is operator posture, out of model.

threats.name: Application-level authorization gaps
threats.description: Tapestry provides no application-level authorization beyond the whitelist and secure-link mechanisms; page-level access control for normal pages, and validation of activation/event context values in handlers, are the application's job.

trustBoundaries.name: HTTP request trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Parameters, form data, activation context, and serialized client state are untrusted until validated. In-model findings are those reachable from an untrusted request before the framework's HMAC/whitelist/escaping controls; findings requiring an unset HMAC passphrase or developer raw output are misconfiguration, out of model.

controls.name: HMAC verification of serialized client state
controls.description: Serialized client state is deserialized only after its HMAC verifies against the configured tapestry.hmac-passphrase, preventing submission of arbitrary serialized objects (the post-CVE-2021-27850 protection).

controls.name: Set a strong HMAC passphrase
controls.description: Set tapestry.hmac-passphrase to a strong secret and protect it like a cryptographic key; without it, the serialized-state protection is void.

controls.name: Fail-closed startup on missing passphrase
controls.description: A startup failure in production mode when the HMAC passphrase is unset is planned (TAP5-2834); currently an unset passphrase is a loud, non-fatal error (logged plus an AlertManager client-side alert).

controls.name: HTML escaping by default
controls.description: Rendered component output is HTML-escaped by default; raw output requires an explicit opt-in via MarkupWriter.writeRaw or the OutputRaw component, where the developer must escape/validate beforehand.

controls.name: Asset path canonicalization and sensitive-extension exclusion
controls.description: Asset URLs resolve only to intended classpath/context resources; traversal is prevented by the servlet container's path normalization plus Tapestry's own checks, including explicit exclusion of sensitive file extensions. The PMC notes these checks could be improved further.

controls.name: Client whitelist analyzer (default LocalhostOnly)
controls.description: @WhitelistAccessOnly resources are served only to whitelisted clients; by default only LocalhostOnly is contributed (localhost IPv4/IPv6). Use it for admin/diagnostic pages and confirm the analyzer fits the deployment. It is an address/origin filter, not user authentication.

controls.name: Secure-link HTTPS enforcement
controls.description: RequestSecurityManager requires HTTPS based on the @Secure annotation, enforced by default in production mode and configurable via the tapestry.secure-enabled symbol. Mark sensitive pages secure and run behind TLS.

controls.name: Built-in CSRF protection
controls.description: The PMC is planning a built-in CSRF module; until then CSRF defence is the application's responsibility (prior art: porscheinformatik/tapestry-csrf-protection).

controls.name: Set upload size and type limits
controls.description: The operator must set upload size/type limits and rely on safe temp-file handling for multipart uploads.

controls.name: Run in production mode
controls.description: Run in production mode; never expose development exception pages or component sources publicly.
